title: Chemical short-range order increases the phonon heat conductivity in a refractory high-entropy alloy

recollection.starting_material: A refractory high-entropy alloy (likely based on Nb-Mo-Ta-W or similar systems), guess
recollection.intervention: Controlled heat treatment to induce chemical short-range order (SRO) without forming long-range ordered phases, guess
recollection.structure: A disordered solid solution with enhanced local chemical ordering (SRO) compared to a fully disordered reference state, guess
recollection.mechanism: SRO reduces phonon scattering by creating a more periodic local potential landscape, thereby increasing the phonon mean free path and thermal conductivity, guess
recollection.results: Significant increase in lattice thermal conductivity (e.g., doubling or tripling) compared to the disordered state, potentially reaching values comparable to pure metals, guess

score.note: The recollection generically identifies inducing SRO but incorrectly proposes heat treatment rather than Monte Carlo-controlled ordering. It mentions only generic local ordering, missing B2-like HfTi/TiZr clusters and percolation pathways. The reduced-scattering/greater phonon mean-free-path mechanism is directionally correct, though it omits reduced lattice distortion, percolation, and phonon-DOS changes. The claimed doubling or tripling is far from the actual ~12% increase.
